title: A decade in perspective
text: Annual diagnoses rose from 9,122 in 2016 to 19,764 in 2025, with a dip in 2020.
limit: The 2026 figures cover part of the year. The revised Q1 and Q2 DOH reports identify 4,633 and 2,994 diagnoses, respectively.

title: Age groups tell a clearer story
text: Ages 25–34 accounted for the largest share of diagnoses. The median age at diagnosis through December 2025 was 28.
limit: Age brackets overlap generations. These data cannot establish a generational effect. The DOH report identifies 182 Q2 diagnoses without age data.

title: Concentration is not prevalence
text: The National Capital Region had the highest cumulative count among the five regions, followed by CALABARZON and Central Luzon.
limit: Cumulative counts cover January 1984 through December 2025. Population figures are needed to compare regional prevalence.

title: Read the categories with context
text: From January 1984 to December 2025, sexual contact accounted for 156,502 of the 163,353 diagnoses in the transmission table.
limit: The reported modes account for 159,601 cases. The remaining 3,752 have no mode listed in this breakdown. These surveillance categories do not indicate identity or individual risk.

title: A different denominator at each step
text: The June 2026 cascade moves from an estimated 288,000 people living with HIV to 159,997 diagnosed, 111,154 on ART, 65,630 tested for viral load, and 63,850 virally suppressed. The suppression percentage applies to those tested.
limit: This aggregate snapshot does not track an individual patient cohort. Stage gaps are not measured dropout. The original figure's 95–95–95 targets are goals, not observed totals.

title: Every count represents a life
text: Of the 352 deaths reported in April–June 2026, 179 were among people aged 25–34.
limit: The counts include deaths from all causes. Calculating mortality rates requires the size of the population at risk.
